wild-strawberries.title: Wild Strawberries
wild-strawberries.syn: Isak Borg (Victor Sjöström), a doctor for fifty years and now nearly eighty, is about to travel back to his old university to receive an honorary degree, accompanied by his daughter-in-law. Along the way he revisits places from his past and remembers. Isak once had a tender first love in his cousin Sara (Bibi Andersson), but his cold and withdrawn nature let his brother step in. Now, sitting on the grass, he recalls the past and sees Sara before him in her white dress. His innate coldness and rationality doomed his marriage; his wife, unable to bear its chill, sought affairs elsewhere. Such a household, together with the inherited coldness, has left his son unwilling to have children and estranged from his own wife. Isak receives his honorary degree, yet remains immersed in heavy self-examination — for an old man near the end of his life, it seems a journey of spiritual redemption.
wild-strawberries.bio: Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish film and theatre director and screenwriter, known for The Seventh Seal, Persona, Cries and Whispers and Fanny and Alexander. He often placed family relationships, questions of faith and the self-scrutiny of his characters in a single story, unfolding inner conflict through faces, dreams and everyday conversation.
wild-strawberries.st: Lead actor Victor Sjöström was himself a major director of the Swedish silent era. By casting this elder as the aging professor, Bergman adds a layer of film history to the on-screen act of looking back. Dreams and reality interweave throughout; watch how the same actor appears across different layers of time.
highlights: Watch how dreams interrupt a clear road route, and how past feelings seep into the present.
Notice the car conversations between the professor and his daughter-in-law: coldness often hides in the most ordinary replies.
honors: 获奖｜1958 Berlin International Film Festival · Golden Bear
获奖｜1960 Golden Globe Awards · Best Foreign Language Film
提名｜32nd Academy Awards · Best Original Screenplay: Ingmar Bergman

dogville.title: Dogville
dogville.syn:
A mysterious woman, Grace (Nicole Kidman), stumbles into a closed, conservative American town. Beautiful and kind, she is fleeing gangsters. Tom, the town's would-be writer, urges the villagers to let her stay and hide for a while, on condition that Grace repays them with farm work. The townspeople agree, but soon learn that Grace is a wanted fugitive. They want to drive her out, and finally agree that she may stay only if she works even harder.

Grace labours day and night, yet cannot escape misfortune. After a police search, one of the townsmen rapes her. It is the start of something ugly: people begin to humiliate her at will, and even Tom drops his kindly mask. Grace is reduced to the town's dog — working, suffering, her kind heart slowly changing. The townspeople never imagine that the woman's mysterious background will turn today's humiliation into their own downfall.
dogville.bio: Lars von Trier is a Danish director and screenwriter and a co-founder of the Dogme 95 movement. His works include Breaking the Waves, Dancer in the Dark and Melancholia. He constantly changes his narrative and filming methods, putting characters in extreme situations to question the limits of compassion, moral judgment and power.
dogville.st: The film was shot on a soundstage, with lines, words and a few props on the floor marking streets and houses. There are no physical walls, yet characters still knock, talk and hide as usual. This near-theatrical treatment of space lets the audience see several corners at once and directs attention to the relationships between people.
highlights: Being able to see every room does not mean the townspeople are willing to see what is happening.
Notice how the residents' wording shifts: demands often arrive in the name of help, risk and fairness.
honors: 入围｜2003 Cannes Film Festival · Main Competition
获奖｜2003 European Film Awards · Best Director: Lars von Trier
获奖｜2003 European Film Awards · Best Cinematographer: Anthony Dod Mantle

sirat.title: Sirāt
sirat.syn: Amid the booming bass of an underground rave, Luis and his son Esteban cross the desert in search of Mar, his daughter and Esteban's sister, who vanished from a party months ago. As they venture deeper into this scorching, chaotic borderland, facing an unfamiliar freedom and a collapsing order, they search not only for family but for themselves. With documentary-textured long takes and silent gazes, the film builds a spiritual journey about limits, faith and family.
sirat.bio: Oliver Laxe was born in Paris, grew up in Galicia, Spain, and lived and filmed for a long time in Morocco. After You All Are Captains, Mimosas and Fire Will Come, he entered the Cannes main competition with Sirāt, continuing to explore people's place in the natural world and their spiritual experience.
sirat.st: The film sets a search for a missing loved one within rave culture and desert roads, with a score by Kangding Ray. The pounding rhythm of electronic music and the vast landscape form a sharp sensory relationship. Notice how sound changes the sense of distance, and why, the deeper the journey goes, the fewer clues the characters can rely on.
highlights: The opening speakers and crowd establish the film's physical feel; listen to the sound as closely as you watch the picture.
Try to avoid detailed plot analyses, so the road, the space and the characters' ordeals keep their original suddenness.

swordsman.title: Swordsman
swordsman.dir: King Hu / Tsui Hark / Ching Siu-tung / Raymond Lee
swordsman.syn:
The imperial vault's martial arts manual, the Sunflower Manual, has been stolen. Gu Jinfu (Lau Shun), the chief eunuch of the Eastern Depot, leads Ouyang Quan (Jackie Cheung) and others south to investigate the retired Embroidered Guard Lin Zhennan, while also enlisting Zuo Lengchan (Yuen Wah), the self-styled leader of the Five Mountains League, as outside support. Linghu Chong (Sam Hui), senior disciple of the Mount Hua school, and his junior Yue Lingshan (Cecilia Yip) are sent by their master to reinforce Lin, but are too weak to help; after receiving Lin's last testament they flee. Along the way they meet Liu Zhengfeng (Wu Ma), the head of the Shunfeng Hall, Qu Yang (Lam Ching-ying), an elder of the Sun Moon Holy Cult, and Feng Qingyang of the Mount Hua school, who teach them the Xiao Ao Jianghu melody and the Nine Swords of Dugu.

All factions converge on Miao territory for the Sunflower Manual. Ouyang Quan and Zuo Lengchan, unable to settle who deserves the credit, disguise themselves as Lin Pingzhi and infiltrate the Mount Hua party. Linghu Chong befriends Ren Yingying (Cheung Man) and Blue Phoenix (Fennie Yuen) of the Sun Moon Cult, and receives their help through his bond with Qu Yang. When Gu Jinfu and Yue Buqun come to blows over the manual, Linghu Chong, unwilling to see his fellow disciples dragged in, unleashes the Nine Swords of Dugu in anger, and finally grasps the true meaning of “laughing proudly through the jianghu.”
swordsman.bio: King Hu built an important aesthetic for Chinese-language wuxia cinema with works such as Dragon Inn and A Touch of Zen. Tsui Hark is a leading figure of the Hong Kong New Wave who has long reshaped genre cinema through directing, producing and writing. This production brought together different creators and bears the marks of old and new wuxia styles meeting.
swordsman.st: The film was begun by King Hu and completed with the participation of Tsui Hark, Ching Siu-tung, Raymond Lee and others. Rather than staging the full novel, it concentrates on the struggle over the manual, sectarian intrigue and personal choices of staying or leaving. Characters move through landscapes, inns and boats, while the song “Laughing Gaily in the Vast Sea” links the encounters and farewells of the jianghu.
highlights: Notice the partnership of Linghu Chong and Yue Lingshan, and the ease and wit Sam Hui brings.
See the jianghu through its songs, bamboo groves and boats: beyond action, the film also builds the atmosphere of people meeting.

swordsman-2.title: Swordsman II
swordsman-2.syn:
Linghu Chong and the Mount Hua disciples prepare to retire from the jianghu, but on the eve of leaving they are once again caught in the strife of the Sun Moon Holy Cult. Dongfang Bubai, who has mastered astonishing martial arts through the Sunflower Manual, faces Ren Woxing, Ren Yingying and others who are trying to take back power in the cult.

Before their positions are clear, Linghu Chong and Dongfang Bubai meet several times in mistaken identity and mutual testing. Personal attraction becomes entangled with conflicts of sect, identity and power, making his wish to leave the jianghu ever harder to fulfil.
swordsman-2.bio: Ching Siu-tung is a Hong Kong action director and martial arts choreographer, best known for the A Chinese Ghost Story series and as action director of Hero and House of Flying Daggers. He excels at combining the speed, power and romance of wuxia through wire work, editing and varied body movement.
swordsman-2.st: This sequel, produced by Tsui Hark and directed by Ching Siu-tung, greatly shifts the focus of the original novel and the first film, placing Dongfang Bubai at the center of the story. Brigitte Lin's performance and costume design, together with Ching's action design, shape the character's aura. It is also well suited to viewing back to back with the first film, to compare how the same jianghu changes its face.
highlights: Notice the exchanges between characters across water, wine and sleeves, where closeness and mistaken identity often arrive together.
Compare the pacing of the first film and its sequel: the ensemble, the action style and the emotional center all change markedly.

leningrad-cowboys.title: Leningrad Cowboys Go America
leningrad-cowboys.syn: The members of the rock band the Leningrad Cowboys look bizarre: huge sunglasses, towering pompadours and outrageous winklepicker shoes are their trademarks. With no hope of success at home, they decide to try their luck in America. On the eve of departure their bassist freezes to death, but the band still packs him into a wooden crate filled with ice and takes him along. A strange mute from their village secretly follows them to New York. Opportunities in New York are not as plentiful as they imagined, and hard times go on. When they have run out of options, they land a gig at a wedding in Mexico. With their last money they buy a used car from an American salesman and head for Mexico, where their final dream awaits…
leningrad-cowboys.bio: Aki Kaurismäki is a Finnish director and screenwriter, known for The Match Factory Girl, The Man Without a Past, The Other Side of Hope and Fallen Leaves. His films use restrained dialogue, spare compositions and deadpan humor to portray work, wandering and mutual care in hard times.
leningrad-cowboys.st: The film places the band in a fictional American road story, and gave the “Leningrad Cowboys” persona a life beyond the screen. Jim Jarmusch makes a cameo as a used-car dealer. The seemingly unflappable characters, set against a tour that keeps changing places and musical styles, create the film’s distinctive comic rhythm.
highlights: See how the exaggerated hairstyles and solemn faces create contrast; many of the jokes don’t rely on dialogue.
Treat each performance as a small culture clash, and notice how the band adapts to the next bar.
honors: 获奖｜1989 Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture · State Quality Prize for Film

turin-horse.title: The Turin Horse
turin-horse.syn: In 1889, Friedrich Nietzsche witnesses a coachman whipping an old horse, and soon after suffers a mental collapse. What actually happened in Turin, in Nietzsche’s mind, in that horse, and in the desperate daily life of the old coachman and his daughter — no one knows.
turin-horse.bio: Béla Tarr is a Hungarian director known for Sátántangó and Werckmeister Harmonies. Through long collaborations with the writer László Krasznahorkai and with editor and co-director Ágnes Hranitzky, among others, he developed a method of depicting people’s predicaments through black-and-white imagery, long takes and continuous ambient sound.
turin-horse.st: The Turin Horse was co-directed by Tarr and Hranitzky, with cinematography by Fred Kelemen and music by Mihály Víg. Tarr announced it as his last feature. The film compresses its narrative into day-after-day labor, letting the wind, the body and the duration of the shot bear the pressure together.
highlights: Notice the subtle differences in the same action on different days; change often matters more than event.
Listen to the wind and the recurring score: sound keeps pressing the outside world into the small interior.
honors: 获奖｜2011 Berlin International Film Festival · Jury Grand Prix (Silver Bear)
获奖｜2011 Berlin International Film Festival · FIPRESCI Prize

a-better-tomorrow.title: A Better Tomorrow
a-better-tomorrow.syn: Sung Tse-ho (Ti Lung), a key member of a Hong Kong counterfeiting ring, and Mark (Chow Yun-fat) are as close as brothers. During a deal in Taipei, Ho is betrayed by his subordinate Shing (Waise Lee), shot and sent to prison. To avenge his brother, Mark goes to Taiwan alone and is beaten into a cripple; his standing in the underworld plummets, and Ho’s father is soon killed. Sung Tse-kit (Leslie Cheung), who had always idolized his brother, learns Ho’s true identity, comes to hate the underworld and him, and vows to use his position as a police officer to wipe out the gangs. After his release, Ho ignores the advice of Mark, who has waited for him in the hope of rebuilding their glory, and resolves to go straight, but Kit will not forgive him. Meanwhile Shing, now a gang boss, wants Ho to work with him again; when refused, he threatens to harm Kit. Driven into a corner, Ho decides to join Mark once more against a formidable enemy.
a-better-tomorrow.bio: John Woo is a Hong Kong director known for The Killer and Hard Boiled, and for Face/Off after his move to Hollywood. He brought the chivalry, promises and sacrifice of wuxia into modern urban action films, letting gunfights carry strong emotional expression.
a-better-tomorrow.st: Produced by Tsui Hark, the film takes up and rewrites the theme of a gangster trying to start anew from Lung Kong’s 1967 film of the same name. Woo places friendship and family side by side, letting each of the three leads face questions of dignity, responsibility and forgiveness. The force of the action also comes from the emotions these relationships build up.
highlights: Notice Mark’s body language, swaggering at his peak and diminished in his fall; the character’s dignity is not conveyed through lines alone.
Connect the pauses and reunions around the gunfights: the action sequences are often the eruption of accumulated feeling.

long-live-the-missus.title: Long Live the Missus!
long-live-the-missus.syn: Chen Sizhen (Chiang Tien-liu), a gracious and capable wife, has managed her household relationships well since marrying Tang Zhiyuan (Zhang Fa). One day her brother Chen Sirui (Han Fei) comes from Taiwan to visit Shanghai and meets Zhiyuan’s sister Tang Zhiqin (Wang Yi), and they fall in love at first sight. But Chen’s father (Shi Hui), who refuses to fund Zhiyuan’s plan to start a company, strongly opposes the match. Sizhen has no choice but to lie that the Tang family has gold bars and cash stashed away, and only then does her father agree to finance the company. Once he gets rich, however, Zhiyuan has an affair with his mistress (Shangguan Yunzhu). To protect her husband’s reputation, Sizhen swallows her grievance. Before long Zhiyuan goes bankrupt, the lie is exposed, and the two families fall out. Sizhen finally decides to divorce Zhiyuan, only to run into Sirui and Zhiqin at the lawyer’s office, where they have secretly registered their marriage. Faced with a couple truly in love, where should Sizhen turn?
long-live-the-missus.bio: Sang Hu was an important director at Wenhua Film Company. He worked with Eileen Chang on Unending Love and Long Live the Missus!, and later directed works such as Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai and The New Year’s Sacrifice. He excelled at developing narratives through character relationships and everyday details, so that light comedy keeps the pressure of real-life obligations.
long-live-the-missus.st: Eileen Chang wrote the original screenplay, concentrating the story within the daily work of an ordinary wife keeping family relations together. The film was shot and released in Shanghai in 1947. Besides the dialogue, notice the qipao, the houses and the social occasions: these details are closely tied to the characters’ class positions.
highlights: See how each kindly smoothing-over leads to the next misunderstanding, with Sizhen always bearing the consequences for others.
Notice the brief pauses after the laughs; the grievance in a domestic comedy often lives in such gaps.
honors: 影史评选｜2005 Hong Kong Film Awards Association · 100 Best Chinese Motion Pictures, No. 82

bullets-over-broadway.title: Bullets Over Broadway
bullets-over-broadway.syn:
For a long time the playwright David (John Cusack) has led an unfulfilled life, and the purity of an artist leaves him disillusioned with today’s corrupt and chaotic theatre world. To please his mistress Olive (Jennifer Tilly), a mob boss takes a liking to the unknown David’s script and offers to invest, on the condition that David casts Olive in the lead. Though Olive’s nagging and wretched acting drive David mad, he painfully gives in before the money. And so a strange company is born.

The holes in the script, the quarrels among the actresses and the leading man’s ever-growing waistline all fill David with despair, but to his surprise, Cheech (Chazz Palminteri), the bodyguard assigned to watch Olive, unwittingly shows a remarkable gift for writing. With Cheech’s help, the rewritten script becomes a huge success; meanwhile, Cheech’s morbid obsession with the play he has written, and the tangled romances within the company, plunge David into another predicament…
bullets-over-broadway.bio: Woody Allen is an American director, screenwriter and actor, known for Annie Hall, Manhattan, Hannah and Her Sisters and Midnight in Paris. He often writes characters’ self-justification, the unease within relationships and an artistic sensibility into comedy, using dense dialogue to unfold the awkwardness of morality and identity.
bullets-over-broadway.st: The film was co-written by Allen and Douglas McGrath. It turns a play’s path from fundraising to rehearsal into a backstage comedy about talent, credit and compromise. Actors, playwright and backers all claim to be protecting the work, but each understands “art” very differently.
highlights: Notice how others react each time Cheech rewrites the script; talent often appears in the least respectable of guises.
Watch the power relations backstage: who pays, who performs and who writes cannot always be kept apart.

green-green-grass.title: Green, Green Grass of Home
green-green-grass.syn:
Lu Danian (Kenny Bee) comes to Neiwan to substitute for his sister, who is about to go abroad, and by her arrangement lodges on the upper floor of the home of the primary-school music teacher Chen Suyun (Jiang Ling). Danian becomes head teacher of Class 4 Zhong. In class, he has to deal with the notorious “Three Musketeers” of mischief-makers, while also caring for Zhou Xingwang (Cheng Chuan-wen), a withdrawn student whose parents have divorced.

Chen Suyun is a quiet girl who comes and goes with Danian all day, and the two grow fond of each other. In Neiwan, people catch fish using poison and electric shocks; Danian resolves to end this practice that seriously damages the natural ecology, launching a “protect the river, protect the fish” campaign at Neiwan Primary School and spreading it across the area. Xingwang’s father Zhou Wen (Tsui Fu-sheng) often goes electric fishing, and mocked by classmates for it, the boy runs away from home. Danian and Suyun set out to bring the child back — and will they finally come together?
green-green-grass.bio: Hou Hsiao-hsien is a major director of the Taiwan New Cinema, known for The Boys from Fengkuei, A Time to Live and a Time to Die, A City of Sadness, The Puppetmaster and The Assassin. He often uses distant views, long takes and restrained narration to present personal experience and historical change within family and local life.
green-green-grass.st: This is one of Hou’s early films starring a pop singer, belonging to his early period along with Cute Girl and Cheerful Wind. It keeps a romantic-comedy thread while giving a good deal of time to children, rivers and village life, and is well suited to comparison with his later works.
highlights: Notice what the children are doing at the edges of the frame; much of the sense of everyday life comes from small actions outside the main plot.
See how the river serves at once as playground, living environment and public issue.

green-green-grass.o: 在那河畔青草青 (Zài nà hépàn qīngcǎo qīng)

blood-simple.title: Blood Simple
blood-simple.syn: On a rainy night, Ray (John Getz) and Abby (Frances McDormand) are having an affair at a hotel. Ray is a bartender, while Abby is the wife of the bar’s owner, Marty (Dan Hedaya). Marty suspects his wife of cheating and hires the detective Visser to investigate. Learning the truth, Marty is furious; he sneaks into Ray’s home to kidnap his wife but is hurt in a scuffle. Marty secretly meets Visser and decides to pay him to kill the two. Visser sneaks into Ray’s home and finds Abby’s revolver. On returning, Visser shows Marty a photograph of the two supposedly killed and, taking advantage of his guard being down, shoots him dead. Ray finds Marty’s body and, mistakenly thinking Abby did it, disposes of it. That night Ray returns to the bar and is stunned to find the faked photograph. Neither Ray nor Abby knows the threat of death is closing in step by step…
blood-simple.bio: Joel Coen and Ethan Coen have long co-written and produced films together. Blood Simple was their feature debut, followed by Fargo, The Big Lebowski, No Country for Old Men, Inside Llewyn Davis and more. They excel at interweaving genre storytelling, black humor and characters’ errors of judgment.
blood-simple.st: The film is credited as directed by Joel Coen and produced by Ethan Coen, with both co-writing. Barry Sonnenfeld’s cinematography, Carter Burwell’s score and Frances McDormand’s screen debut already make a distinct presence in this early work. Neon, interior light and sound keep changing what the audience knows.
highlights: Keep track of what the audience knows versus what the characters think they know; suspense comes from the gap between the two.
Notice the doors, windows, lighting and off-screen sound; they often reveal danger earlier than dialogue.

spring-in-a-small-town.title: Spring in a Small Town
spring-in-a-small-town.syn:
Around 1948, in an ordinary southern Chinese town where broken walls and ruins are everywhere, the young wife Zhou Yuwen (Wei Wei) lives a dull life with her sickly husband Dai Liyan (Shi Yu). The war has cost Liyan not only his family property but also his faith in life. Yuwen’s days consist of going out in the morning to buy vegetables and fetch Liyan’s medicine, pacing along the town wall for a long while, then returning home despondent; she drops the medicine off with a word or two and spends most of the rest of the day sitting in the room of Liyan’s younger sister Dai Xiu (Zhang Hongmei), embroidering and sighing alone — apart from the wall where she wanders each morning, that room is the only lively place in town for her.

The arrival of Zhang Zhichen (Li Wei) breaks the deathly stillness. He is Liyan’s old friend, and also Yuwen’s former lover. In contrast to Liyan’s gloomy listlessness, Zhichen is young, healthy and full of life, and Dai Xiu, an outsider in this little town, quietly develops feelings for him. But Zhichen has never forgotten Yuwen, and he is undoubtedly what Yuwen longs for and calls to in her heart. As Zhichen and Yuwen play out their psychological game of advancing and retreating, “feelings expressed but restrained by propriety,” Liyan and Dai Xiu glimpse its outline.
spring-in-a-small-town.bio: Fei Mu was a Chinese film director whose works include Human Nature (Tianlun), The Blood of Wolf Mountain and Spring in a Small Town, as well as the Peking opera film Sheng si hen (Regret for Life and Death). He valued the film’s overall atmosphere, the psychological rhythm of its characters and spatial relationships, and Spring in a Small Town is also an important work for understanding the poetic expression of Chinese cinema.
spring-in-a-small-town.st: The film organizes feeling through Yuwen’s voice-over, letting what she says of her heart run parallel to the action before our eyes. The story unfolds around a few characters in a limited space, with emotion often expressed through walking, pauses, dissolves and the distance between people. The ruined town wall and house also take part continuously in the changing relationships.
highlights: Listen to how Yuwen’s narration precedes, accompanies or departs from her actions; words and body are not always in agreement.
Notice the distances between characters at doors, windows, corridors and the town wall: restrained movement carries feelings that are anything but calm.
honors: 影史评选｜2005 Hong Kong Film Awards Association · 100 Best Chinese Motion Pictures, No. 1

mon-oncle.title: Mon Oncle
mon-oncle.syn: Monsieur Hulot (Jacques Tati) comes from the countryside to stay with his sister (Adrienne Servantie) in Paris. He cannot get used to the modern appliances in her home and is constantly thrown into a flap. Fortunately, his young nephew Gérard likes this uncle and goes everywhere with him; Gérard likewise dislikes the modern gadgets at home, so Hulot takes him to play at an old house in the suburbs. Hulot’s brother-in-law, Monsieur Arpel (Jean-Pierre Zola), finds him a job at his factory, but Hulot cannot adapt to modern machinery either, botches many things and causes many laughs. Fed up, his brother-in-law decides to send him off with another job elsewhere, and Hulot happily says goodbye to his nephew, taking it as the end of an unusual holiday…
mon-oncle.bio: Jacques Tati was a French director, actor and comedic creator best known for the screen character Monsieur Hulot. His works include Monsieur Hulot’s Holiday, Mon Oncle and Playtime. His comedy relies on physical movement, spatial staging and sound, turning everyday settings into a stage that rewards patient observation.
mon-oncle.st: This was Tati’s first feature in color and the second Monsieur Hulot film. It contrasts the modern house, the factory and the old quarter, with sound design and composition carrying a great deal of the humor. You needn’t watch only the lead: a figure deep in the frame or off to the side may be completing a small comedy of their own.
highlights: Notice the sounds of the fountain, footsteps and machines: sound often voices the absurdity of the environment before the characters do.
Divide your attention to the edges and distance of the frame; Tati often places several gags in the same space.
honors: 获奖｜1958 Cannes Film Festival · Special Jury Prize
获奖｜31st Academy Awards · Best Foreign Language Film

where-is-the-friends-house.title: Where Is the Friend’s House?
where-is-the-friends-house.syn: In a primary school in a remote Iranian mountain village, a group of children listen to their teacher in class. While checking homework, the teacher finds that Mohammad Reza has repeatedly failed to complete his, and scolds him severely, saying he will be expelled if it happens again. The teacher stresses that this is to help them build good discipline. After school, the little boy Ahmad discovers that he has taken his seatmate Mohammad’s notebook home by mistake. Having understood the teacher’s earnest admonition, Ahmad knows this notebook is Mohammad’s proof of being able to continue in class. To return the notebook, Ahmad hopes his mother and grandfather will help, but both fail him. So he can only set out alone to the village in the mountains across the way to find his seatmate. But since he does not know where his friend lives, he meets obstacles everywhere and encounters unimaginable difficulties…
where-is-the-friends-house.bio: Abbas Kiarostami was an Iranian director and screenwriter whose works include Close-Up, Taste of Cherry and The Wind Will Carry Us. Where Is the Friend’s House?, together with And Life Goes On and Through the Olive Trees, forms the “Koker trilogy,” which revisits the same place and way of life in different ways.
where-is-the-friends-house.st: The film is the starting point of the Koker trilogy, following a child’s search for the owner of a notebook through a single day. It does not advance on a complex plot; instead, roads, questions, waiting and repeatedly going the wrong way build tension. In the process, the rules of the adult world reveal their distance from the child’s sense of responsibility.
highlights: Notice whether adults actually answer the child’s question; a mismatch in communication is often more agonizing than refusal.
Watch the recurring mountain path, doors and corners, and how the terrain turns a small matter into an adventure.

the-sacrifice.title: The Sacrifice
the-sacrifice.syn: The critic Alexander (Erland Josephson) celebrates his fiftieth birthday at his home in Sweden; his young son, who has just had throat surgery, cannot speak. In silence, the two plant a sapling, hoping it will sprout green branches. But that same evening, the radio broadcasts news of a nuclear missile launch: the Third World War is about to break out. In despair Alexander prays to God that war not happen, even vowing to give up everything he has to stop the apocalypse. Longing for the world to be reborn, and in a state of utter exhaustion, Alexander sets fire to his own house. Amid the roaring blaze, he is taken to hospital by ambulance. His young son goes to the shore to keep watering the sapling they planted together, and everything seems calm again.
the-sacrifice.bio: Andrei Tarkovsky was a Soviet director whose seven feature films include Ivan’s Childhood, Andrei Rublev, Solaris, Mirror, Stalker, Nostalghia and The Sacrifice. He also wrote Sculpting in Time, and explored human spiritual life through sustained shots, natural elements and spaces of memory.
the-sacrifice.st: The Sacrifice is Tarkovsky’s last feature, shot in Sweden with cinematography by Sven Nykvist and starring Erland Josephson. The film sets one day in a family against questions about destruction, faith and giving, and many key passages unfold through the characters’ movement and long periods of waiting.
highlights: Notice where characters stand inside the house and in the landscape; action in the distance can shift the center of an entire scene.
Watch the dead tree, the child and the recurring sounds together; the vow in the film continues through concrete action.
honors: 获奖｜1986 Cannes Film Festival · Grand Prix of the Jury
获奖｜1986 Cannes Film Festival · FIPRESCI Prize

faces-places.title: Faces Places
faces-places.syn: Agnès Varda, the “grandmother of the French New Wave,” and the street artist JR travel through the villages of France in a small van. Along the way they photograph the people they meet, then paste billboard-sized portraits onto the walls of houses and factories.
faces-places.bio: Agnès Varda was a French film director and visual artist whose works include Cléo from 5 to 7, Vagabond and The Gleaners and I. JR is a French artist known for giant photographic projects in public spaces. This film lets cinema and street photography join together in looking at ordinary people.
faces-places.st: In their Cannes interview, the two explained that the collaboration began as nothing more than a short rural film project, and then kept extending as encounters accumulated. They did not write the plot in advance, but first chose a place or a theme, then let the people and events on site shape the shooting. The easy conversation in the film also comes from this way of working together.
highlights: Notice how the subjects see their own faces and surroundings anew once the giant photographs are pasted up.
Watch how the two authors tease and observe each other, until the creators themselves slowly become the ones being recorded.
honors: 获奖｜2017 Cannes Film Festival · L’Œil d’or (Golden Eye) for Best Documentary
获奖｜2018 Independent Spirit Awards · Best Documentary
提名｜90th Academy Awards · Best Documentary Feature
入选｜2017 Cannes Film Festival · Out of Competition Screening

john-wick.title: John Wick
john-wick.syn:
John Wick, a top assassin retired for years, has just lost his wife, who left him a puppy before her death to help him through the hardest days. The son of a Russian crime boss covets his sports car, breaks into his home, beats him up, takes the car and kills the puppy.

John, who once struck fear into the whole underworld, picks up his guns again. For a dog and a promise, he fights his way through the gang’s nightclub, church and docks, and the Continental Hotel, a sanctuary built for assassins, opens its doors to the audience for the first time.
john-wick.bio: Chad Stahelski came up through martial arts and the stunt industry; he was Keanu Reeves’s stunt double in The Matrix, and later co-founded the action-design company 87eleven with David Leitch. John Wick was his directorial debut, and he has since directed all four main entries of the series, continuing to influence Hollywood action films with long takes, real close-quarters combat and gunplay design.
john-wick.st: Made by creators from a stunt-team background, the film uses long takes and medium shots extensively for its action, letting the audience see every close-quarters fight and every reload, a style dubbed “gun-fu.” The script by Derek Kolstad builds, on a minimalist revenge story, an assassins’ world with its own rules, currency and hotel. The film had never before played in mainland China cinemas; this is the first time the series’ opening film reaches the big screen on the mainland.
highlights: Notice the complete actions in each gunfight: reloads, disarming at close range and follow-up shots are all clearly shown on camera.
The Continental Hotel, the gold coins and the rule of “no business on the grounds” are the starting point of the entire John Wick universe.

happy-birthday.title: Happy Birthday
happy-birthday.syn:
Eight-year-old Toha works as a child maid in a wealthy household in Cairo. She has grown up with the employers’ daughter Nelly and become her closest playmate. Nelly’s birthday is near, and Toha, who has never had a birthday herself, is determined to throw her the perfect party, as if it might give her a share of happiness too.

As she grows closer to Nelly’s mother Layla, the line between master and servant begins to blur. But the nearer the party gets, the more clearly Toha realizes that she belongs neither to this family nor to this party. The whole story takes place within a single day.
happy-birthday.bio: Sarah Goher is an Egyptian-American director and screenwriter who has worked as a producer and director on Marvel’s series Moon Knight. Happy Birthday is her feature debut, co-written with Mohamed Diab; it won several major awards at its Tribeca premiere and was Egypt’s submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film.
happy-birthday.st: The film observes Cairo’s class order through a child’s eyes: the employers’ kitchen, living room and party scene are completely different worlds for Toha within the same house. The filmmakers compress the whole story into a single day, letting the preparations for a birthday party slowly expose the tension between child labor, class and intimacy. The young actress Doha Ramadan stars.
highlights: Follow Toha’s line of sight: which rooms she may enter and what she may not touch say more about her situation, and earlier, than any dialogue.
Notice the few moments when Toha and Layla grow close; tenderness and the employment relationship remain entangled throughout.

linka-linka.title: Linka Linka
linka-linka.syn:
Sangye, a young director who has spent many years in Beijing, returns to Lhasa to recreate her girlhood in her first feature. As shooting inches forward, the unresolved knot between her and her father, and what once happened to her childhood friend Lhamo, begin to resurface.

A chance reunion makes the two girls’ different memories of the same past collide head-on. The film moves back and forth between the shoot and memory, linking three summers through a single night. The title, “Linka,” refers to the Lhasa tradition of picnicking in the woods in summer.
linka-linka.bio: Kangdrun is a Tibetan screenwriter and director. Her short film Orlo with Karma, focused on Lhasa’s younger generation, was selected for the 2025 FIRST International Film Festival and the Vancouver International Film Festival. Linka Linka is her feature debut and has taken part in the Shanghai International Film Festival’s Project Market training camp and WIP section, and the FIRST Film Festival’s WIP market.
linka-linka.st: Shot in Lhasa and Shanghai from 2020, the film is described as the first feature focused on contemporary urban life in Tibet. The filmmakers use a film-within-a-film structure, letting Sangye’s shooting and real memories interfere with each other, and ask about the instability of memory and “whose version counts as truth.” Most of the roles are played by non-professional actors.
highlights: Notice the switches between the shoot and flashbacks: the same summer is not the same in different people’s mouths.
Lhasa summers, linka picnics and young people’s daily lives are a contemporary Tibetan life rarely seen on the big screen.
honors: 入围｜2025 Tokyo International Film Festival · Asian Future
获奖｜2026 Hong Kong International Film Festival · Firebird Award, Young Cinema Competition (Chinese Language)
获奖｜2026 Hong Kong International Film Festival · FIPRESCI Prize
获奖｜2026 Buenos Aires International Festival of Independent Cinema · Best Cinematography
入选｜2026 Shanghai International Film Festival · New Chinese Wave

kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.title: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.syn:
On the day of her wedding rehearsal, a pregnant bride is gunned down by her former assassin crew, the Deadly Viper Assassination Squad, shot in the head and left in a coma for four years. When she wakes, she draws up a list: O-Ren Ishii in Tokyo, Vernita Green in Los Angeles, Budd and Elle Driver in the desert, and last, her former lover Bill.

This time Tarantino recombines Kill Bill, once released in two parts, into a single complete film, running from the snowy blood-soaked fight at the House of Blue Leaves all the way to the final conversation in Mexico.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.bio: Quentin Tarantino is an American director and screenwriter whose works include Reservoir Dogs, Pulp Fiction, Inglourious Basterds, Django Unchained and Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. He has won the Palme d’Or at Cannes and two Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay. His films are known for non-linear narratives, extensive genre homage and highly distinctive dialogue.
kill-bill-whole-bloody-affair.st: Tarantino originally conceived Kill Bill as a single film, then split it in two because of length, released in 2003 and 2004. The Whole Bloody Affair is the version he has in mind as complete: the two parts combined, the anime sequence expanded by Production I.G., and given its first nationwide theatrical release in North America in December 2025. The mainland China version runs about 275 minutes as listed on ticketing platforms; what exactly has changed in the mainland version has not been announced.
highlights: Watch both volumes in one sitting: the Eastern martial-arts flavor of the first half and the Western tone of the second turn within a single film.
Notice the expanded anime sequence, which gives O-Ren Ishii’s background a fuller account than the original.

the-odyssey.title: The Odyssey
the-odyssey.syn:
After the Trojan War, Odysseus, king of Ithaca, sets out on the sea route home, only to be punished by the gods and repeatedly blocked by monsters and temptations, a journey that lasts ten years.

Far away in Ithaca, his wife Penelope and son Telemachus struggle to hold the palace against a crowd of suitors coveting the throne. Adapted from Homer’s epic, it tells how a man passes through an entire mythic world to return to his own home.
the-odyssey.bio: Christopher Nolan is a British-American director and screenwriter whose works include Memento, The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar and Dunkirk, and who won the Academy Awards for Best Picture and Best Director for Oppenheimer. He has long insisted on shooting on film and in IMAX, favoring practical locations and effects.
the-odyssey.st: The Odyssey is the first narrative feature shot entirely with IMAX film cameras, using more than two million feet of IMAX 70mm film. Because each roll lasts only about three minutes, longer scenes require stopping midway to change magazines. Nolan adapted the script himself, and the film was released in North America on July 17, 2026.
highlights: Shot entirely on IMAX film; if you can choose an IMAX auditorium, do.
Two lines advance in alternation: Odysseus at sea and Penelope in Ithaca, each guarding the same idea of “coming home.”

dune-part-three.title: Dune: Part Three
dune-part-three.syn:
The story takes place seventeen years after Dune: Part Two. Paul Atreides has become emperor of the universe, and the holy war launched in his name sweeps the entire empire.

The greater his power, the narrower the future he can see. The Tleilaxu Face Dancer Scytale secretly plots to overthrow him, and court, religion and prophecy interweave into a new conspiracy. Adapted from Frank Herbert’s novel Dune Messiah, it is the finale of Villeneuve’s Dune trilogy.
dune-part-three.bio: Denis Villeneuve is a Canadian director whose works include Incendies, Prisoners, Sicario, Arrival and Blade Runner 2049. His two-part Dune has won both acclaim and box-office success worldwide, as well as several technical Academy Awards.
dune-part-three.st: Unlike the first two films, which were shot entirely on IMAX-certified digital cameras, the third was shot mainly on 65mm film, with some passages on 15/70mm IMAX film, and the desert scenes on IMAX-certified digital cameras to convey the harshness of the environment. The script was adapted by Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan. The runtime has not been officially announced.
highlights: As the finale of a trilogy, it is best to catch up on Dune and Dune: Part Two first.
Pay attention to Robert Pattinson’s Face Dancer Scytale, who is key to this installment’s conspiracy line.

avengers-doomsday.title: Avengers: Doomsday
avengers-doomsday.syn:
Fourteen months after the events of Thunderbolts*, heroes from three universes must band together: the Avengers of Earth-616, Wakanda and the new Avengers, the Fantastic Four of Earth-828, and the original X-Men from another universe.

They face a threat officially classed as “existence-level”: Doctor Doom. Robert Downey Jr. returns to Marvel, this time as the villain.
avengers-doomsday.bio: The brothers Anthony Russo and Joe Russo are American directors and producers who directed Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Captain America: Civil War, Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. Their company AGBO took part in producing this film.
avengers-doomsday.st: This is the main Avengers sequel following Avengers: Endgame and the 39th film of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, written by Michael Waldron and Stephen McFeely. Shooting began in April 2025 at Pinewood Studios in the UK; it was originally set for release in May 2026, then pushed to December 18. The follow-up, Avengers: Secret Wars, is scheduled for December 2027.
highlights: Robert Downey Jr. turning from Iron Man into Doctor Doom is one of the film’s biggest draws.
The Fantastic Four and the original X-Men share the screen with the Avengers for the first time; it helps to first catch up on The Fantastic Four: First Steps and Thunderbolts*.

we-live-in-time.title: We Live in Time
we-live-in-time.syn:
Almut is a former figure skater and now a chef; Tobias has just been through a divorce. An unexpected car accident brings the two together, and they fall in love, move in, and quarrel over whether to have a child.

Almut is diagnosed with ovarian cancer and goes into remission after treatment, and the two have a daughter, Ella. When the cancer returns, she decides to enter the Bocuse d’Or world cooking competition. The film scrambles chronology, leaping back and forth between meeting, giving birth and saying goodbye, to piece together a ten-year love.
we-live-in-time.bio: John Crowley is an Irish director who came from the theatre, known for Brooklyn (nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture) and The Goldfinch, and who has also directed numerous productions in London’s West End and on Broadway. He excels at delicate emotion and the staging of performances.
we-live-in-time.st: The script is by the British playwright Nick Payne, who uses non-linear narrative to cut different points in the same relationship together, letting the audience live through the decade in jumps, the way memory works. The film had its world premiere at the 2024 Toronto International Film Festival and was shown as the closing film (out of competition) of the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival.
highlights: The timeline is shuffled: use hairstyles, the kitchen and the daughter’s age to judge which year each scene takes place.
Florence Pugh did her homework for the chef scenes, and the cooking competition is the emotional high point of the whole film.
honors: 入选｜2024 Toronto International Film Festival · World Premiere
入选｜2024 San Sebastián International Film Festival · Closing Film (Out of Competition)

for-better-or-worse.title: For Better or For Worse
for-better-or-worse.syn:
Li Xinran, an actress once plagued by depression, meets Piao Yuanbo, who has just left monastic life, at a party celebrating his return to lay life. They fall in love, marry, have their first child, and begin a new life with a few million yuan in savings.

Inexperience and extravagance whittle the savings away bit by bit. Yuanbo stakes all his hope on a handpan instrument factory in the mountains of Anji, but a second child is born, a partner leaves and the debts keep growing. Quarrels and reconciliations take turns, and the two learn, in the mire, to let go of their imagination of a perfect life.
for-better-or-worse.bio: Qin Xiaoyue is a Chinese documentary director and screenwriter. Her earlier film Nest records a family’s parting and reunion and won Best Documentary Feature at the FIRST International Film Festival. She is used to following ordinary families for long periods, paying attention to strength and vulnerability within intimate relationships.
for-better-or-worse.st: The film records the couple through long-term following, with the director also taking part in the filming, calling it “an extremely exhausting and extremely thrilling shoot.” The filmmakers neither romanticize marriage nor judge who is right or wrong; instead they let the audience see how two people struggle and compromise together. The film was in the main competition of the 2025 FIRST International Film Festival.
highlights: This is not a fiction film: the quarrels, reconciliations and silences really happened; notice how close the camera is to the two.
The rise and fall of the handpan factory is an undercurrent that moves almost in step with the course of the marriage.
honors: 提名｜2025 FIRST International Film Festival · Best Documentary Feature

resident-evil.title: Resident Evil
resident-evil.syn: Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier, is given a job to deliver a shipment into Raccoon City. When he arrives, a virus is spreading out of control and the whole city falls overnight, mutated monsters hunting the living in the streets. Trapped in the catastrophe, Bryan can only look for a way out amid the chaos and try to get out alive.
resident-evil.bio: Zach Cregger is an American director, screenwriter and actor, first known as a member of the comedy troupe The Whitest Kids U’ Know. His self-written and self-directed horror films Barbarian (2022) and Weapons (2025) made him one of the most closely watched genre directors of recent years; Resident Evil is his new video game adaptation.

no-mobile.title: No Mobile
no-mobile.syn: In the winter of 2023, the artist Hao Yang left his phone at home and set out alone on a 134-day offline journey through China. With only paper maps, cash, letters and face-to-face conversation, he traveled through 68 cities and counties in 24 provincial-level regions. Facing ubiquitous QR codes, reservations and online payments, he ran into one unexpected obstacle after another, and also rediscovered trust and chance encounters between people. The film records this personal experiment with digital daily life, asking how we perceive the world when life no longer depends on screens.
no-mobile.bio: Hao Yang works in contemporary art, using painting, moving image, calligraphy and walking as his media. He studied and researched art in the UK, and from 2023 to 2024 completed a 134-day trip across China with no phone and no internet, which he developed into a documentary and non-fiction writing.
no-mobile.st: The director answers a daily life surrounded by digital systems with 134 days of offline wandering: going without a phone and the internet meant layers of obstacles in payment, transport and lodging, and also brought the possibility of chance encounters, concentration and a renewed sense of time. The director Hao Yang will join the audience for a conversation after this screening. The film runs 14:30–16:21 on October 31; the post-screening talk begins at 16:21 and is expected to end at 17:20.
highlights: When everything defaults to needing a QR code, how does an offline journey continue?
134 days, 24 provincial-level regions, 68 cities and counties: a practice about technology and personal freedom.
October 31, 16:21–17:20: post-screening Q&A with the director Hao Yang in person.
honors: 入围｜2025 Sweden Film Awards · Finalist (as stated on the poster)
入围｜2025 Austin International Art Festival · Finalist (as stated on the poster)
入选｜2025 Internationales Festival Zeichen der Nacht · Official Selection (as stated on the poster)

style-kaleidoscope.name: Style Kaleidoscope
style-kaleidoscope.blurb: From Bergman’s road memories to Tarkovsky’s apocalyptic prayer, from Fei Mu’s city wall to Tsui Hark’s jianghu, seventeen works spanning 1947 to 2025 share one screen — a map of “style.”

cinema-2026.name: Now Showing
cinema-2026.blurb: The new releases and re-releases worth heading to the cinema for this autumn and winter: Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, shot entirely on IMAX film; Tarantino’s Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair; John Wick, finally released in mainland China; the Tribeca-winning Egyptian film Happy Birthday; and the Tibetan director Kangdrun’s Linka Linka; plus We Live in Time, the documentary For Better or For Worse, and year-end blockbusters Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three. Screenings vary — please check each cinema’s ticketing platform.

sparrow-tribe-space.name: Sparrow Tribe Film Space
sparrow-tribe-space.blurb: Sparrow Tribe is an independent screening and curating collective, best known over the past decade for its “blind-box screenings.” After four quiet years, it set out again around National Day 2026 with a single-screen offline arthouse space of its own: Sparrow Tribe Film Space. This page collects the space’s screening schedule and will be updated as sessions are announced.
